items.title: Marcos disappointed Philippines halted Bataan Nuclear Power Plant
items.description: More than four decades after the Bataan Nuclear Power Plant was mothballed, President Marcos expressed disappointment that the facility was halted, as he claimed that people are now concerned about having access to affordable electricity, regardless of its source.

items.title: Romualdez allowed to sign court order in jail
items.description: The Sandiganbayan Third Division has granted the request of former speaker Martin Romualdez to sign a court order on Oct. 12 while in detention at the New Quezon City Jail.

items.title: Senators weigh in on Mark Villar’s majority bloc move
items.description: Senators from the majority bloc weighed in on the move of Sen. Mark Villar to bolt the Alan Peter Cayetano-led minority to join them in the ruling coalition in the upper chamber.

items.title: ICC allows 7 additional incidents in Duterte case
items.description: Trial judges of the International Criminal Court have allowed prosecutors to include additional incidents in the crimes against humanity case against former president Rodrigo Duterte.

items.title: PAF to acquire advanced Black Hawk training systems
items.description: The Armed Forces of the Philippines is acquiring an advanced virtual training and maintenance system from US-based Lockheed Martin for its growing fleet of 31 Black Hawk helicopters.

items.title: Recto to agencies: Speed up El Niño spending, procurement
items.description: Malacañang has ordered government agencies to accelerate spending and preparations for the expected “Super El Niño,” which could intensify in the coming months and persist through the first half of next year.

items.title: Senate court takes break for budget deliberations
items.description: Senators will take a break from their duties as impeachment court judges this week so they can focus on deliberating the proposed budget and having it approved before the year ends.

items.title: Ombudsman, GSIS inspect Jinggoy’s office
items.description: The Office of the Ombudsman and the Government Service Insurance System have inspected detained Sen. Jinggoy Estrada’s stripped Senate office, with the former looking into possible legal violations and the latter checking the structural integrity of the dismantled space, Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian confirmed yesterday.

items.title: Pope OKs Tagle as first Asian dean of cardinals
items.description: Pope Leo XIV has approved the election of Filipino Luis Antonio Cardinal Tagle as dean of the College of Cardinals, making him the first Asian prelate to hold the position and placing him among the Church’s key figures in the process of choosing the next pope.

items.title: Marcos accepts DICT chief’s resignation
items.description: President Marcos has accepted the resignation of Henry Aguda as secretary of the Department of Information and Communications Technology, according to Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla.

items.title: With power bills already high, Meralco wins approval to raise own fees after 15 years
items.description: After its first rate review in 15 years, Meralco has won regulatory approval to raise its distribution charges even after already posting a record P51.13 billion in profits in 2025
